title: Mavericks sign Naji Marshall to 3-year, $52.5 million contract extension: Source
content:
The Dallas Mavericks are making sure Naji Marshall isn’t going anywhere.

Marshall, the slashing forward nicknamed “The Knife,” has agreed to a three-year, $52.5 million contract extension that could keep him in Dallas through the 2029-30 season, a league source told The Athletic on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly about the contract.

Marshall, 28, is coming off a career-best season in which he averaged 15.2 points on 51 percent shooting to go along with 4.7 rebounds and 3.3 assists over 74 games.

Marshall signed with Dallas in the summer of 2024 after spending the first four years of his career with the New Orleans Pelicans. In his two-year Dallas tenure, Marshall has consistently shown the ability to get into the paint and finish but has struggled with his outside shot, converting below 30 percent from 3 each of the past two seasons.

The Mavericks received significant trade interest in Marshall in February, but they chose to hold onto him. Now, the team’s new Masai Ujiri-led front office has decided it wants to keep Marshall around long-term.

Marshall had one year remaining on his contract worth $9.4 million before agreeing to this extension.

“Naji has earned this opportunity through the way he approaches the game every day,” Ujiri said in a statement. “He is a competitive player who impacts winning in a variety of ways. His versatility, toughness and willingness to embrace every challenge make him an important part of what we’re building.”

The Mavericks have had a busy offseason. They hired Dusty May as Jason Kidd’s coaching replacement. Then Dallas walked away from the first round of the NBA Draft in June with Morez Johnson Jr. and Sergio De Larrea. The team then acquired Marcus Sasser, Tarik Biberović, Santi Aldama and Zaccharie Risacher via trade.

The Mavericks, who have 16 players signed to standard contracts, still need to make a move to whittle their roster down to 15 before the start of this season.

With Kyrie Irving set to return to the court this fall, the Mavericks are hopeful they can make a significant improvement coming off last season’s 26-win campaign. Marshall should be a big factor in that effort. His contract extension will pay him an average of $17.4 million per season — a handsome sum for a player who entered the NBA as an undrafted free agent in 2020.
